cultural.vision_reason: This is a studio portrait of named Brulé (Sicangu) Lakota/Sioux chiefs and women in traditional dress with dentalium ornaments, feather bonnet, pipe, and blanket; Lakota is a closely related division of the Sioux alongside Dakota, so the image is acceptable evidence of the broader Sioux cultural group's dress and regalia even if the museum label specifies the Lakota (not Dakota) branch.

physical.title: photographic print (black and white); album
physical.summary:
Photograph (black and white) from an album; studio portrait of Two Strike's wife, Two Strikes (Nomkahpa) a Brulé (Sicangu) Lakota chief, Susie Yellow Horse, Iron Shell (Ma--zah-pon-kes- kah) a Brulé (Sicangu) Sioux chief, the wife of Spotted Tail, Spotted Tail (Sinte Gleska) a Brulé (Sicangu) Lakota chief, Swift Bear (Ma-to-lousah) a Brulé (Sicangu) Lakota chief, and a White man; Two Strike's wife is seated wearing a cloth patterned dress, dentalium ear ornaments, and a woven blanket on her knees, her hair is in two braids and she is holding a fan; Two Strike is standing wearing a warrior shirt, a neck tie and a bone breastplate, his hair is in two bunches wrapped in cloth and he has a feather in his hair; Susie Yellow Horse is seated wearing a cloth patterned dress, a dentalium choker, and dentalium and abalone ear ornaments, she has a wool blanket over her knees, and her hair is in two braids; Iron Shell is standing wearing an eagle feather trailer warbonnet, and a wool cape; Spotted Tail is seated wearing a western-style shirt and waistcoat, a peace medal, metal ear ornaments, moccasins, and a blanket over his knees, half of his hair is in a bunch wrapped in fur; Swift Bear is seated wearing a western-style shirt, waistcoat and trouser, a dentalium choker and a blanket over his knees, he is holding feathers and a hat is at his feet; the White man is seated wearing a suit and hat; St Louis, United States of America 
Albumen print
